pr.title: Ignore intrinsic calls in cross-crate-inlining cost model
pr.description:
I noticed in a side project that a function which just compares to `[u64; 2]` for equality is not cross-crate-inlinable. That was surprising to me because I didn't think that code contained a function call, but of course our array comparisons are lowered to an intrinsic. Intrinsic calls don't make a function no longer a leaf, so it makes sense to add this as an exception to the "only leaves" cross-crate-inline heuristic.

This is the useful compare link: https://perf.rust-lang.org/compare.html?start=7cb1a81145a739c4fd858abe3c624ce8e6e5f9cd&end=c3f0a64dbf9fba4722dacf8e39d2fe00069c995e&stat=instructions%3Au because it disables CGU merging in both commits, so effects that cause changes in the sysroot to perturb partitioning downstream are excluded. Perturbations to what is and isn't cross-crate-inlinable in the sysroot has chaotic effects on what items are in which CGUs after merging. It looks like before this PR by sheer luck some of the CGUs dirtied by the patch in eza incr-unchanged happened to be merged together, and with this PR they are not.

The perf runs on this PR point to a nice runtime performance improvement.

classification.name: Inline
evidence: fn run_pass(&self, tcx: TyCtxt<'tcx>, body: &mut Body<'tcx>) {

The PR changes the cross_crate_inlinable query, which is not itself a MirPass, but tracing the affected caller shows it controls the Inline pass's inlining cost model. NormalInliner::check_callee_mir_body calls tcx.cross_crate_inlinable(callsite.callee.def_id()) to choose the higher inline_mir_hint_threshold instead of the normal threshold. Ignoring rustc_intrinsic calls in the leaf/cost check makes more intrinsic-only callees cross-crate inlinable, changing which callees Inline inlines. ForceInline's inlining decision path does not use this changed query, so only Inline is justified.

analysis.originalLogic: In the cross-crate inlining cost model that feeds the `Inline` pass's cross-crate-inlinability heuristic, `CostChecker` treated every MIR `Call` terminator as making the callee non-leaf: `TerminatorKind::Call { unwind, .. } => { ... self.calls += 1; ... }`. Consequently, a callee whose optimized MIR contains only a call to an intrinsic—such as an array equality comparison lowered to an intrinsic—was counted as having a call and could fail the "only leaves" cross-crate-inline heuristic.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation is the old cost-model behavior: count `TerminatorKind::Call` terminators unconditionally toward `self.calls`, including calls whose callee resolves via `func.const_fn_def()` to a definition carrying the `rustc_intrinsic` attribute. That treats intrinsic-only callees as non-leaf, suppresses their cross-crate inlinability, and therefore prevents the `Inline` pass from cross-crate-inlining them. The merged change instead returns early before `self.calls += 1;` when the callee is an intrinsic, because intrinsics have no body assigned to a CGU.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR functions visited by the cross-crate inlining cost checker, specifically `TerminatorKind::Call` terminators and their callee definitions. The distinguishing domain is callees containing calls only to `#[rustc_intrinsic]` functions versus callees containing ordinary non-intrinsic calls; input examples include cross-crate functions comparing `&[u64; 2]` values for equality.
analysis.summary: The cross-crate inlining cost model counted intrinsic calls as ordinary calls, making intrinsic-only leaf functions non-cross-crate-inlinable. The merged change ignores calls to definitions carrying the `rustc_intrinsic` attribute when computing the leaf/call cost, allowing the Inline pass to cross-crate-inline functions whose optimized MIR only calls intrinsics.
analysis.trigger: A cross-crate callee's MIR has a `TerminatorKind::Call` whose callee resolves through `func.const_fn_def()` to a `DefId` carrying `sym::rustc_intrinsic`, and the function has no other non-intrinsic calls that would keep it out of the leaf/cross-crate-inlinable heuristic.
preconditions: The terminator being examined must be `TerminatorKind::Call`; the callee must resolve through `func.const_fn_def()`.
The resolved callee `DefId` must carry `sym::rustc_intrinsic`; otherwise the call must still increment `self.calls`.
The changed decision applies to cross-crate inlining cost modeling; `ForceInline` follows a separate decision path and is not justified by this change.
pitfalls: Do not ignore all calls: only calls whose callee is a `const_fn_def` with the `rustc_intrinsic` attribute are exempt.
Returning early for an intrinsic call also skips the landing-pad accounting for that terminator, so changes involving `UnwindAction::Cleanup` should not automatically use the same exemption.
Changing which functions are cross-crate-inlinable perturbs CGU partitioning; unrelated assembly/codegen tests may start inlining the function under test and no longer observe its intended body.

The PR description notes that changes in what is cross-crate-inlinable in the sysroot have chaotic downstream CGU-merging effects, so codegen differences outside the direct test can be noise rather than evidence of a different transformation.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a cross-crate auxiliary function whose optimized MIR contains an intrinsic-only call, for example `pub fn leaf_with_intrinsic(a: &[u64; 2], b: &[u64; 2]) -> bool { a == b }`, then test from the caller crate that `Inline` inlines it: define `#[no_mangle] pub fn leaf_with_intrinsic_outer(...) -> bool { leaf::leaf_with_intrinsic(a, b) }` and check with `// CHECK-NOT: call {{.*}}leaf_with_intrinsic`. Retain a contrast such as `// CHECK: call {{.*}}stem_fn` for a non-leaf function. For tests that must observe a function body rather than an inlined copy, add `#[inline(never)]` so the changed heuristic cannot inline it.
